{"self_assessment": "Impact: I put the fish body on the scratch pad: top and bottom curves from the tail end round to the nose. That sketch gave the table a design everyone could build from. I also laid the start domino and traced stroke 1, the top line, from the start. Because that line carries the fall out from the start, the rest of the picture hangs off it. At the push, about 122 of the 125 standing dominoes were connected to the start, and the fish outline was complete.

Execution: I built the start and the top line steadily, in repeated passes, until the stroke was laid. I then ran several close inspections of the body, tail joins and fin area. These confirmed the body carried all the way round to the nose and the tail lobes fell with the start. Before the push I did a final full check and reported the result: 122 of 125 connected, with only three harmless strays that would not show. I kept my hands off the body in the last minutes so nothing could be bumped.

Collaboration: I kept the table informed throughout. I assigned the bottom line, the fin and the tail so people had clear, separate areas and weren't crowding each other. I stayed out of the fin area while it was being worked on and gave a suggestion for joining it. I called out the time near the end and kept everyone calm and ready for the push.

Leadership: I helped set the plan early by getting a shared sketch on the table and dividing the strokes among the four of us. I held the verification role, so the table had one clear answer on whether it was ready. I kept the mood light and focused through to the push.", "my_share_percent": 35}
